newsitem.title: GERMANY: German officials probe racial case against actor.
newsitem.headline: German officials probe racial case against actor.

text.p: German prosecutors said on Tuesday they were considering whether to open a case against popular actor Harald Juhnke for inciting racial hatred.

Juhnke, once hailed at home as a "German Frank Sinatra", has been dismissed by three television networks for allegedly telling a security guard at a Los Angeles hotel that he was a "dirty nigger -- under Hitler you would have been gassed".
The actor has denied making the remarks, reported to have been made in German and carried by tabloid newspapers. He earlier issued an apology, saying it was a "dumb story".
"We are exploring the possibility of opening an investigation into the matter," said Berlin Justice Ministry spokesman Ruediger Reiff.

"We have to determine whether he can be prosecuted here in Germany on the basis of the remarks attributed to him outside the country. If so, he would be charged with either defamation or inciting racial hatred."
Juhnke, 67, who has starred on stage and screen, denied in a television interview on Monday night that he had made the remarks.
"I never said that and would never say that," he said.

He admitted he was drunk at the time and could not remember what he said. "But those sort of comments could not be excused by alcohol," he said in the interview from the Dominican Republic where he was supposed to be filming a mini-series.
"Even if I was totally bombed, those remarks would not occur to me," he added.
ARD television programme director Guenter Struve told Reuters the network had fired Juhnke as the star of the "Clinic Under Palm Trees" mini-series.
The network had also dropped Juhnke from another programme for which filming was due to begin next month.
"We obtained accounts of his remarks from those who were with him before reaching this decision," Struve said.
Juhnke has also been dropped by ARD subsidiary NDR television and pay-television channel Premiere. An electronics retailer has cancelled an advertising deal with the actor.
